definitions.name: Redis Count Existing Keys (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Count Existing Keys. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Delete Keys (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Delete Keys. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Unlink Keys (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Unlink Keys. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Key Type (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Key Type. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Key TTL Seconds (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Key TTL Seconds. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Append Stream Entry (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Append Stream Entry. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Stream Length (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Stream Length. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

/*
 * Vendored from `cluster-key-slot@1.1.2`
 * (https://github.com/invertase/cluster-key-slot), patched to fix a
 * disagreement with real Redis servers over how an empty hash tag ("{}") is
 * handled.
 *
 * Redis treats an empty hash tag as no tag at all: given `{}` it hashes the
 * whole key and stops searching (see `keyHashSlot()` in Redis's
 * `src/cluster.c`). The upstream single-pass scanner instead falls through
 * and keeps scanning for the next `}`, hashing whatever sits between --
 * which can silently misroute commands and sharded pub/sub subscriptions to
 * the wrong node. Vendoring was necessary because the upstream repository

definitions.name: Redis Read Stream Range (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Read Stream Range. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Read Stream Reverse Range (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Read Stream Reverse Range. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Read Stream Once (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Read Stream Once. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Read Consumer Group Once (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Read Consumer Group Once. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Acknowledge Stream Entries (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Acknowledge Stream Entries. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Delete Stream Entries (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Delete Stream Entries. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Trim Stream (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Trim Stream. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Create Consumer Group (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Create Consumer Group. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Destroy Consumer Group (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Destroy Consumer Group. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Set Consumer Group ID (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Set Consumer Group ID. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis List Pending Entries (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Pending Entries. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: Redis Claim Pending Entries (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Claim Pending Entries. Uses vetted Redis commands through embedded @redis/client@6.3.0, direct TCP or verified TLS. Configure host/port/database and passwordSecret (default REDIS_PASSWORD), optional username and caSecret, or builtin $connection RuntimeConnection config/credentials. TLS defaults require; disable is explicit. One operation deadline starts before asynchronous profiles/secrets/module loading; no reconnect/offline replay and $retries must be 0. Mutations require request.confirm=true. Results preserve exact integer text, ordered values, explicit null and binary hex; no provider bodies or credentials in errors. A failure may have committed effects: inspect Redis before a deliberate retry. SCAN COUNT is a hint; oversized pages reject. Transactions queue <=50 vetted scalar-returning commands and cannot roll back EXEC errors; an EXEC error can follow committed commands. Streams are bounded nonblocking one-shot operations with explicit XACK and no automatic acknowledgement; pending entries remain caller-managed. No Pub/Sub/listener/blocking commands, scripting, flush/config/admin, cluster/sentinel or distributed lock guarantee. Sources: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/connect/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/produsage/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/using-commands/transactions/ https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/streams/ https://github.com/redis/node-redis/tree/redis%406.3.0

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.
